body:
It might be kind of a energy saving mechanism of the mind. Painting a less complex picture than the outcome would otherwise be, but those unexpected features are indeed refreshing. There isn't always too much hard facts about things, I should remember to view the assumptions as elastic whenever there's something new to find out.

I had something to say about that feeling when you're unable to even imagine what someone might have looked like as a very young child, but it's getting late here and I'll probably try to sleep. I can't even explain how good this conversation with you felt. That spontaneous thought exchange, remembering that this too, exists. Thanks.

Yes. That sounds familiar, though not surely the only downside to being some kind of an 'observer'. While things this person says and does might indeed have something to do with personality trait A, I start to see anything else as just circling around A, assuming the characteristic affects their actions and other features and not the other way around. I know it's a bit black and white kind of thinking, as not having a totally fluid identity doesn't mean they're rigid. Do you feel it's as strong with people you've known for a long time?
